chunks: As for what ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan narrated from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿĀmir and Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about what is lawful for a man from a menstruating woman. He said: “Nothing, until she becomes pure.”

So the intended meaning in his statement, “Nothing,” is that it is to be understood as meaning that nothing is lawful for him of intercourse in the private part, even though what is less than that is lawful for him. And the first two possible interpretations that we mentioned in the previous reports are also possible in this report.

key_terms.لَا شَيْءَ: nothing is lawful, in the specific legal sense being discussed

ai.seo_question: What is permissible for a husband with his wife during menstruation according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling concerning what is permissible between a man and his wife while she is menstruating. The apparent wording is clarified to mean the prohibition of intercourse in the private part, while acts short of that remain possible according to the contextual interpretation mentioned by the compiler.
